subject: Segregation evidence envelope: annotated network topology and control-plane/data-plane separation
messages:
From: Maria Stein <maria.stein@nordicbank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: nordicbank-secops@nordicbank.com
Date: 2026-09-15T12:12:00Z
Subject: Segregation evidence envelope - initial ask

Hi Hannah / Laura,

Thanks for taking this — NordicBank's SOC 2 team needs a focused packet showing how Redwood isolates Dedicated and Private deployments from a network and control-plane perspective. Specifically we need: 

- An annotated topology that clearly labels control plane vs data plane connectivity for Dedicated nodes, Private VPCs, and any edge components.
- Egress controls: how outbound traffic is filtered, NAT/gateway patterns, and common egress destinations.
- KMS/Key boundary note: where customer keys live, what crosses the boundary, and KMS APIs used.
- A short list of evidence artifacts (diagrams, audit logs, config snippets) and expected timelines.

I've attached our RFI (NordicBank_Security_RFI_v1.pdf) with the preferred format. Ideally we get a first-draft diagram and checklist by EOD tomorrow CET so our internal reviewers can triage.

Appreciate you looping in anyone else who owns the topology.

Best,
Maria Stein
Senior InfoSec Manager | NordicBank
attachments: NordicBank_Security_RFI_v1.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Stein <maria.stein@nordicbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Segregation evidence envelope - initial ask

Maria — thanks for the clear ask and the RFI. We'll assemble a compact "segregation envelope" that maps exactly to your bullets. Quick plan: 

1) Kimberly creates the annotated topology (control-plane vs data-plane overlays) and exports an architecture PNG + printable PDF.
2) Rishi pulls example egress ACLs and a short KMS boundary note (API endpoints and where keys are hosted for Private deployments).
3) I'll put together a one-page checklist tying each RFI item to the artifact we provide and add traceability to SOC 2 controls.

Can you confirm the scope — is this limited to Dedicated and Private (no hosted/shared-tenant flow required)? That will change a couple of diagrams.

Deliverables target: draft diagram + checklist + 2 supporting PDFs within 24 hours. If that timeline is tight, please let us know which items to prioritize.

Thanks — looping Kimberly and Rishi for visibility.

--
Hannah Schmitt
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Maria Stein <maria.stein@nordicbank.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T20:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Segregation evidence envelope - initial ask

Team — attaching the first-pass artifacts. Notes inline.

Attachments: segregation-envelope-diagram-v1.png; controlplane-dataflow-notes-v1.pdf; segregation-checklist.xlsx

Highlights: 
- Diagram (PNG) uses layered overlays: blue = control plane (orchestration, control API endpoints, management plane subnets), green = data plane (inference GPU pools, customer data plane VPCs). Each hop is labeled with whether traffic is mutual-TLS and whether it's allowed over private interconnect or public egress.
- Control-plane isolation: our control plane sits in a separate management VPC with strict peering to Dedicated pools via private endpoints. For Private deployments we run a local control plane proxy that communicates outbound over an mTLS tunnel to the customer's control plane mirror (diagram shows the proxy boundary).
- Egress: outbound traffic from Dedicated pools egress through a managed NAT gateway with FQDN filtering at the application layer and network-level ACLs. For Private, egress is customer-managed; we document recommended firewall rules and provide sample iptables/nsg snippets in the PDF.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys for Private deployments are held in the customer's KMS (diagram annotated). Hosted keys for Dedicated are stored in a Redwood-managed KMS cluster; calls to the HSM/KMS are restricted to control-plane subnets.

Open items / requests for Maria: 
- Confirm whether you need packet-capture evidence for a sample connection (we can provide redacted PCAPs).
- Confirm if you want route tables and exact ACL entries or a redacted example.

I also added a short checklist spreadsheet to map each item to the RFI section. If Hannah agrees, I'll fold in our SOC 2 control IDs and export a printable packet.

- Kimberly
Principal Security Architect | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Maria Stein <maria.stein@nordicbank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, nordicbank-secops@nordicbank.com
Date: 2026-09-16T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Segregation evidence envelope - initial ask

Hannah / Kimberly — thanks, this looks good as a start and matches the level of detail our reviewers want. A few clarifications before we close the loop: 

- Packet captures: yes, a single redacted PCAP showing the mTLS handshake between a control-plane proxy and Redwood's management endpoint would be helpful. Please include timestamps and the redaction approach used.
- Route tables: a redacted example is sufficient. Please ensure the redaction preserves destination prefixes (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16 -> 10.0.0.0/16) but removes internal hostnames/IPs.
- KMS proof: for Private, a short statement describing the customer KMS flow plus an example KMS policy snippet will be enough.

If you can deliver those three bullets, we should be able to move this into our SOC 2 evidence tracker. I'll assign to our reviewer on receipt and confirm by EOD CET.

Thanks again — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Maria Stein
Senior InfoSec Manager | NordicBank
